summary: Katelyn Lesse leads the Claude Developer Platform team at Anthropic and presents how the platform is evolving to help developers build powerful agentic systems. She organizes the talk around three strategic pillars. First, harnessing Claude's capabilities: the API exposes features like extended thinking (with configurable token budgets) and tool use (both built-in tools like web search and custom tools defined by name, description, and input schema). Claude Code is used as a recurring example, demonstrating how these features work in practice for debugging, file operations, and test execution. Second, managing Claude's context window: context management is critical but complex, especially for coding agents dealing with codebases, instructions, and tool calls. Anthropic introduced MCP (Model Context Protocol) a year ago for standardized interaction with external systems. A memory tool allows Claude to store context outside the window and retrieve it when needed. Context editing clears old tool results that consume space without aiding later responses. Combining memory and context editing yielded a 39% performance improvement on internal evals. Some models now support million-token context windows, and Claude is being trained to understand its remaining context space. Third, giving Claude a computer: Anthropic believes in letting Claude work autonomously in sandboxed environments. The code execution tool provides a secure sandbox where Claude can write and run code on Anthropic's servers. Agent skills, combinable with MCP, provide domain expertise through folders of scripts, instructions, and resources that Claude selectively invokes. Looking ahead, Anthropic will continue evolving the API as Claude's capabilities grow, expand memory and context management tools, and invest further in agent infrastructure addressing orchestration, secure environments, and sandboxing. Lesse concludes by announcing that Anthropic is actively hiring across end product design, developer relations, and other functions.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Platform Vision
sections.summary: Katelyn Lesse introduces herself as leader of the Claude Developer Platform team and frames the talk around helping developers build powerful agentic systems, using Claude Code as the primary example product.

sections.title: Harnessing Claude's Capabilities
sections.summary: Covers extended thinking with configurable token budgets and tool use (built-in and custom) as API features that expose Claude's trained capabilities. Claude Code is used to illustrate both features.

sections.title: Managing Claude's Context Window
sections.summary: Discusses MCP for external system interaction, a memory tool for storing and retrieving context outside the window, and context editing for clearing old tool results. Combining memory and context editing yielded a 39% performance improvement on internal evals. Million-token context windows are mentioned.

sections.title: Giving Claude a Computer
sections.summary: Covers the vision of letting Claude work autonomously in sandboxed environments. Describes the code execution tool, the Claude Code on web and mobile launch challenges (security, container orchestration, session persistence), and agent skills combinable with MCP. A follow-up talk on skills is mentioned.

sections.title: Future Platform Evolution and Hiring
sections.summary: Lesse outlines three forward directions: evolving the API as Claude's capabilities grow, expanding memory and context management tools, and investing further in agent infrastructure for orchestration, security, and sandboxing. She concludes by announcing Anthropic is hiring across end product design, developer relations, and other functions.
